intro: This is a mantra from the **Yajurveda** (Yajurveda, Purnamadah (Isha Upanishad invocation)). Below are the Sanskrit text and a **plain English meaning**.
takeaways: The four Vedas are Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda and Atharvaveda.
Vedic mantras are learned by listening and repeating.

p: **ॐ पूर्णमदः पूर्णमिदं पूर्णात्पूर्णमुदच्यते । पूर्णस्य पूर्णमादाय पूर्णमेवावशिष्यते ॥ ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः ॥**
That is whole, this is whole. From the whole the whole arises. Take the whole from the whole and the whole remains.
The Yajurveda is one of the four Vedas, the oldest scriptures of Sanatana Dharma, handed down by voice for thousands of years.

faq.a: That is whole, this is whole. From the whole the whole arises. Take the whole from the whole and the whole remains.
There are **four**: Rig, Yajur, Sama and Atharva.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering.
